answer: Every claim must cross a karst of trust: once filed, the lottery casts it into an ocean of strangers, and a random established witness has a day to inspect it and co-sign with a lotus seal. The desk checks the seal before paying; if the claim proves fake, claimant and witness both lose their standing. One honest user needs one witness, while 1,000 fakes would need 1,000 separate witnesses willing to risk their own standing — a gap near 1,000 to 1. When one operator filed fifty claims hoping for friendly witnesses, the lottery scattered them across the ocean, and every claim was refused.
